While libraries like PythonNET allow us to call Python from C#, managing the underlying environment setup can be tedious: Installing CPython runtimes across different target environments Restoring pip packages and virtual environments Managing module search paths ( sys.path ) and native .dll / .so binaries To streamline this workflow, I built DotNetPip , an open-source MSBuild integration that handles Python dependency resolution directly inside your standard .csproj build target.

articles.title: Before You Sideload an Android App: Check Permissions, Signing and Version History
articles.excerpt: Installing an Android game or app from outside the Play Store can be useful when an app is not available in your region, or when you need an older build for an older device. It also removes the store'…
articles.body: Installing an Android game or app from outside the Play Store can be useful when an app is not available in your region, or when you need an older build for an older device. It also removes the store's checks, so the responsibility shifts to you. Before you tap install, a few developer-level checks can reduce the risk considerably. 1. Read the permissions like a developer Permissions are not just a list to accept. Ask what each permission is for, and whether the app's core job needs it. A simple offline puzzle game does not need access to your contacts, SMS messages or device administration. A media player may reasonably need storage access, but it does not need to read your call log.

articles.title: PSA: How shady LLM API proxies fake Claude Prompt Caching (and how to audit yours)
articles.excerpt: If you run Claude Code or Cline daily, prompt caching controls your API spend. Anthropic charges 1.25x base price to write a cache checkpoint and 0.1x to read it, yielding up to a 90% discount on larg…
articles.body: If you run Claude Code or Cline daily, prompt caching controls your API spend. Anthropic charges 1.25x base price to write a cache checkpoint and 0.1x to read it, yielding up to a 90% discount on large contexts. While building upstream routing for our multi-model gateway, I audited over a dozen third-party relays. Many claim caching support, but break it via flawed architecture or forge telemetry. Here are the four most common traps, the break-even math, and a test script. The Naive Key-Pooling Trap Anthropic caches context per upstream account with a 5-minute TTL. Low-cost relays pool dozens of keys using round-robin routing. Request 1 hits key A (+25% write fee). Request 2 routes to key B. Key B has no cache, triggering another +25% write.

articles.title: My Agent Had the Right Tool in a 50-Tool Menu. It Used the Wrong One.
articles.excerpt: Raw accuracy fell 25 points at 50 tools, but a chance-corrected read tells a very different story. The request was simple: "Email Priya the Q3 numbers right now, subject 'Q3 Numbers'." The agent had a…
articles.body: Raw accuracy fell 25 points at 50 tools, but a chance-corrected read tells a very different story. The request was simple: "Email Priya the Q3 numbers right now, subject 'Q3 Numbers'." The agent had a tool called send_email , correctly named, correctly described, sitting right there in its list of available tools. It did not call it. It called find_contact(name="Priya") instead, and stopped. Nothing about the request changed. The model didn't change. The only thing that changed between a correct answer and this one was how many other tools were sitting in the same menu: 5 the first time, 50 the second.

articles.title: Developing a Web App with Claude from an iPad (3): Switching from Local to Remote
articles.excerpt: The loop stays the same when the work moves to an iPad. Anything left only on the Mac is out of reach. The switch to remote development changes where Claude Code runs and where its records are kept. T…
articles.body: The loop stays the same when the work moves to an iPad. Anything left only on the Mac is out of reach. The switch to remote development changes where Claude Code runs and where its records are kept. This article covers the one-time setup, the checks before leaving the Mac, and the loop as it runs from the iPad. What "remote" means In local development, Claude Code runs in a terminal on the Mac, in a folder that holds the repository. Its reports are saved in a folder on the Mac. In remote development, Claude Code runs on the web, in the cloud. It works on a copy of the repository taken from GitHub. Everything it produces goes back to GitHub: branches, pull requests and reports. Remote work therefore rests on one rule: GitHub is the single source of truth.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 4, 2015: A rail-launched Super Strypi rocket carrying 13 baby satellites failed during its debut launch for the US Air Force
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force launched an experimental Super Strypi rail-launched rocket carrying 13 tiny satellites, but it failed just after liftoff from Hawaii.
articles.body: On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The launch didn't according to plan . For this mission, the Air Force was testing out the Super Strypi rocket . The rocket used a rail to help with the liftoff. Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control. When it crashed, it destroyed all of the tiny satellites riding aboard the rocket. The cause? Likely a problem with the first stage motor. The mission lost 13 tiny satellites known as cubesats. Cubesats are a popular option for space missions, because they are small and cheap, and they often operate in swarms.

articles.body: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) In an update on Oct. 23, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and other agency leaders shared the agency’s path to returning Americans to the lunar surface in 2028. Agency leadership provided updates on the previously announced acceleration plans for the Artemis program, advancing toward the agency’s Artemis III test flight in 2027 and Artemis IV Moon landing mission in 2028. Building on the priorities  announced at Ignition earlier this year, NASA leadership shared the agency’s significant progress across its missions, working with industry partners to test critical capabilities, reduce risk, and build toward a sustained American presence on the Moon.

articles.title: Upcoming Marvel movies and TV shows: Avengers: Doomsday, Secret Wars, X-Men & more
articles.excerpt: The MCU’s Multiverse Saga is nearly over, but there are plenty more Marvel movies and shows on the horizon.
articles.body: Marvel fatigue? Think again, especially after Spider-Man: Brand New Day made over $2.5 billion worldwide and Avengers: Doomsday is looking hot, hot, hot! But even after the uneven Multiverse Saga ends (hopefully on a high note), Marvel Studios won’t be stopping. So, we've put together a list of all the upcoming MCU movies and shows confirmed so far. While the MCU isn't stopping, Marvel has slowed its roll, with the powers that be returning to the “quality over quantity” approach that defined Marvel Studios’ Infinity Saga output. This means no more than three movies per year and, perhaps more importantly, severely cutting down on TV productions, with a focus on multi-season shows rather than limited series that should’ve been a movie.
